title: Replace Subclass with Delegate

solutions.title: One TermPricing, a plan object standing in for the subclass
solutions.tradeoff: TermPricing takes a TermLengthPlan as a constructor argument instead of the length being baked into a type name, so a caller can no longer tell a standard term from an intensive one by asking what class an object is - it has to read the plan's numbers or a label the code did not have to carry before.

reviewFocus: Is the category-discount switch written in exactly one place in the solution, or did one copy survive under a different name?
Is TermPricing still declared abstract anywhere, or does the solution's class construct directly with `new TermPricing(plan, category)`?
Do StandardTermPricing and IntensiveTermPricing still exist as files or exported names anywhere in the solution?

Does the walkthrough name the second axis explicitly - student category - and show why it could not be added as a third subclass dimension without multiplying classes, rather than just asserting delegation is nicer?

Compare against drill-12-11: that drill also reaches for a delegate, for the opposite reason - a superclass whose bequest was mostly refused, not a subclass whose axis ran out of room. Does this walkthrough state its own test for reaching for a delegate, distinct from 12-11's, rather than leaning on the shared word?
